questions.enonce_markdown: Draw a well labelled diagram of the internal structure of a villus. *(9 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Diagram to draw:** a large **longitudinal section through a single villus** of the small intestine (ileum), with the title "Longitudinal section of a villus".

What to draw:

- A **finger-like projection** with a rounded top, rising from the intestinal wall into the lumen.
- On the outside, a **single layer of epithelial (columnar) cells**, with tiny **microvilli** (brush border) on the free surface and a few **goblet cells** (mucus) between them.
- In the centre, a **blind-ended lymph vessel, the lacteal**, running along the middle of the villus.
- A **network of blood capillaries** close to the epithelium, linked to a small **arteriole** (bringing blood in) and a **venule** (taking blood out) at the base.
- A few **muscle fibres** and connective tissue in the core, which shorten the villus.
- At the base, the **crypt of Lieberkuhn** (intestinal gland) opening between neighbouring villi.

**Labels expected:** lumen of the intestine, epithelium (single layer of cells), microvilli (brush border), goblet cell, blood capillary network, lacteal (lymph vessel), muscle fibre, arteriole, venule, connective tissue, crypt of Lieberkuhn.

questions.enonce_markdown: State six (6) ways in which herbivorous mammals are adapted to their diet. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Incisors** are chisel-shaped and sharp, and cut against a **horny pad** (in ruminants, the upper incisors are absent) to cut off grass and leaves.
2. A **gap (diastema)** between the incisors and the premolars allows the tongue to move food around.
3. **Premolars and molars** are broad with **ridged, flat surfaces** to grind tough plant material, and the jaw moves **sideways** in a grinding action.
4. **Long digestive tract (long small intestine)**, giving enough time for the digestion and absorption of tough plant food rich in cellulose.
5. A large **caecum and appendix** (e.g. in rabbits and horses) containing **symbiotic bacteria** that produce **cellulase**, which digests cellulose.
6. **Ruminants** have a **stomach with several chambers** (rumen) where bacteria digest cellulose, and they **chew the cud** (regurgitate and chew again).
7. Rodents and some herbivores have **continually growing teeth** which replace the wear caused by grinding.
8. **Eyes at the sides of the head** give a wide field of view to detect predators while feeding.

(Any six points.)

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the fate of the end products of photosynthesis? *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The end products of photosynthesis are **glucose** and **oxygen** (with water as a by-product).

**Fate of glucose:**
1. It is used in **respiration** to release energy for the cell.
2. It is converted into **starch** and stored temporarily in the leaf, or for long periods in roots, tubers, stems and seeds.
3. It is changed to **sucrose** and transported through the **phloem** to growing and storage regions.
4. It is used to make **cellulose** for new cell walls.
5. With **nitrates and other mineral salts** from the soil, it is used to make **amino acids and proteins**; it can also be converted into **fats and oils** (e.g. stored in seeds).

**Fate of oxygen:** part is used in the respiration of the plant cells; the rest **diffuses out through the stomata** into the atmosphere.
